title: Colour and grade
purpose: Measures palette, luminance range, saturation, temperature and consistency, and turns them into a reproducible grade recipe.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F6 statistics per shot, F7 waveform and vectorscope on 3+ representative frames, F9 for accent colours.
pitfalls: Reporting a palette dominated by a text panel as the grade
Comparing colours across differently compressed frames
Calling a look 'cinematic' instead of measuring it

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.text: one technique description, at most 300 characters, no copied content
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F6: Per-frame colour statistics (YMIN, YAVG, YMAX, SATAVG, HUEMED, UAVG, VAVG): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=$WORK/stats.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.F7: Scopes: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "format=yuv444p,waveform=display=overlay" "$WORK/wave_T.png"; vectorscope with -vf "format=yuv444p,vectorscope=mode=color3"
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1

questions.question: What are the video's dominant colours, ordered by area?
questions.how_to_answer: Merge evidence.shots[].palette weighted by shot duration (video_re_palette_per_shot); keep up to 8 colours, merging colours within about 20 RGB units.
questions.challenge: Check that a persistent panel or title colour is not reported as the scene grade; F9 on two shots should contain the top colours.

questions.question: How would the grade be described in measurable terms (temperature, contrast, saturation, black and white points)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills visual.grade as a short technique description.
questions.how_to_answer: Summarise 003-006 in one sentence with the numbers, for example 'warm (V-U +12), moderate contrast (Y 18-232), saturated (SATAVG 72)'.
questions.challenge: Words like 'cinematic' or 'moody' are taste; each adjective must carry a number.

questions.question: What is the average saturation (signalstats SATAVG), median over shots?
questions.how_to_answer: F6 on 1 s of each shot (or a sample of 10 shots); median of per-shot SATAVG means.
questions.challenge: Text panels and bright titles raise SATAVG; recompute on a crop without text for 3 shots.

questions.question: What are the luma black and white points (median YMIN and YMAX per shot)?
questions.why_it_matters: Defines contrast range for the grade recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YMIN/YMAX per sampled shot; report medians.
questions.challenge: Tiny specular highlights set YMAX; also report the 1st/99th percentile from a histogram if available.

questions.question: Are blacks crushed, natural, or lifted (faded look)?
questions.how_to_answer: From YMIN medians and F7 waveforms: as a rough convention, lifted when the darkest areas stay above about 30 (8-bit, limited range 16-235) and crushed when large areas sit flat at 16. Report the values.
questions.challenge: Check the stream colour range in A7; full-range sources shift these values.

questions.question: Is the colour temperature warm, neutral or cool on average?
questions.how_to_answer: F6 UAVG and VAVG medians (128 is neutral in 8-bit): V clearly above U suggests warm, U above V cool (this swarm uses a difference of 4 as the cut-off; report the values); confirm on an F7 vectorscope.
questions.challenge: Content colours (a blue ocean) shift averages without any grade; check neutral elements (white text) with F9.

questions.question: How consistent is the grade across shots (standard deviation of per-shot SATAVG and HUEMED)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells whether the format normalises sources to one look.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 per shot; report stdev of SATAVG and of HUEMED (circular).
questions.challenge: Different subjects vary naturally; compare against a deliberately mixed baseline is impossible, so mark the conclusion inferred.

questions.question: Is there a teal-and-orange split (cool shadows, warm highlights)?
questions.how_to_answer: F7 vectorscope: two lobes near orange and teal; F9 on shadow and highlight areas.
questions.challenge: Skin tones and sky alone create both lobes; check a frame without people or sky.

questions.question: What accent colour is used for emphasis (highlighted words, labels, arrows)?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 inside highlighted words and labels in 3 places.
questions.challenge: Report the spread across samples.

questions.question: Does each item get its own colour code (label colour, tint, background hue)?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 on labels and backgrounds per item.
questions.challenge: Hue differences under about 20 degrees are not distinct codes.

questions.question: Is the title colour complementary to, analogous to, or independent of the scene palette?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a title colour selection rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Hue of the title colour (F9) versus dominant scene hues (001).
questions.challenge: Report hue angles.

questions.question: Do skin tones look natural, warmed, cooled or stylised?
questions.why_it_matters: Constrains the grade when people appear.
questions.how_to_answer: F7 vectorscope: skin falls near the skin-tone line; F9 on skin areas.
questions.challenge: Do not describe the people; only the colour position.

questions.question: Are shadows and highlights tinted differently (split toning), and with which hues?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 on dark and bright neutral regions; hue of each.
questions.challenge: Report the samples and their hues.

questions.question: How strong is edge darkening (corner luma divided by centre luma)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills vignette strength in the grade.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 luma of corner versus centre on 3 even frames.
questions.challenge: Pick frames where the content is even.

questions.question: Does overall brightness change across the video (darker or brighter toward the end)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a brightness arc rule or confirms a flat grade.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG per shot against time; slope.
questions.challenge: Content-driven changes (night scenes) do not imply a grade arc.

questions.question: Is the hook graded differently from the body?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare F6 stats for hook shots against item shots.
questions.challenge: Require a difference beyond the between-item spread.

questions.question: Is there film emulation (grain plus halation plus faded blacks)?
questions.how_to_answer: Combine grain (layers lens), lifted blacks (005) and red halos around highlights (F3).
questions.challenge: All three cues must be present for 'true'.

questions.question: Is the look high-key, mid-key or low-key (median YAVG)?
questions.how_to_answer: Median F6 YAVG; this swarm's convention is high-key above about 150 and low-key below about 80 (8-bit limited range). Report the value.
questions.challenge: State the thresholds used and the value.

questions.question: What share of pixels are clipped at the top of the range in typical frames?
questions.how_to_answer: F7 waveform shows a flat line at the top; or count pixels with Y at max using a histogram on 3 frames.
questions.challenge: White text is intentionally at max; exclude text areas.

questions.question: Is the palette tied to the topic (derived from the subject) or a fixed brand palette?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare palettes across items: fixed colours present in all items suggest a brand palette.
questions.challenge: A single-topic video cannot separate the two cleanly; mark inferred.

questions.question: How many distinct dominant hues does the video use?
questions.how_to_answer: Cluster palette colours by hue (30-degree bins); count bins holding at least 5% of area.
questions.challenge: Greys have no hue; exclude low-saturation colours from the count.

questions.question: Are there monochrome, duotone or desaturated sections, and when?
questions.how_to_answer: F6 SATAVG near zero over a shot.
questions.challenge: Black-and-white archival photos are content, not grade; check whether colour graphics are also desaturated.

questions.question: Are neon or glowing colours used (very high saturation with glow)?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 samples with SAT near max and a glow halo on F3.
questions.challenge: Report the saturation values.

questions.question: What ffmpeg filter recipe approximates the observed grade (for example eq, colorbalance, curves, vignette)?
questions.how_to_answer: Choose filters and values to match 003-006; render 3 test frames from neutral test media and compare F6 statistics.
questions.challenge: Run the recipe on a test frame; stats must move in the stated direction.

questions.question: Which colour parameters should a new video set (palette, accent, saturation, temperature)?
questions.how_to_answer: Collect 001, 003, 006 and 009 into parameters.
questions.challenge: Each parameter needs derived_from.

questions.question: What colours do gradient overlays use, and in which direction do they run?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 at both ends of visible gradients.
questions.challenge: Give the two end colours and the direction.

questions.question: How saturated are text colours compared with the scene (text SAT vs scene SATAVG)?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 on text versus F6 scene averages.
questions.challenge: Report both values.

questions.question: Are archival or historical images given a special treatment (sepia, grain, frame)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a treatment for archival material.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect shots with old photographs.
questions.challenge: If no archival material exists, answer not determinable.

questions.question: Are there colour flashes at beats or transitions, and which colour?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds flash colour to the transition recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: F6 YAVG spikes over one or two frames; F9 colour on the flash frame.
questions.challenge: Check against the transitions lens.

questions.question: Is extra sharpening or clarity applied (halos at edges)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds or rules out a sharpen step.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 enlarged crops at high-contrast edges; bright or dark halos 1-3 px wide indicate sharpening.
questions.challenge: Compression ringing looks similar; check a smooth gradient region too.

questions.question: Are different source images colour-matched (white balance consistent across shots)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a colour-matching step in the render plan.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 on neutral (white or grey) areas across 5 shots; compare U/V.
questions.challenge: Report the U/V values per shot.

questions.question: Is there visible banding in gradients (8-bit steps), and should the rebuild add dither or grain?
questions.why_it_matters: A quality rule for generated gradients.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 enlarged crop of a smooth gradient; count visible steps.
questions.challenge: Banding from the platform's re-encode is not the creator's technique; note the uncertainty.
